reconcile.connective: Defenders account for the closing 'thirty and seven' by tallying the three classes (3 + 2 + 32) and reading 'the thirty' as a corps title, not a literal headcount.

discrepancy.connective: The objection is pressed by Steve Wells in The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, who counts only thirty-six names in the roster against the text's own stated total of thirty-seven.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.work: The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "How many mighty men did David have?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/mighty-men.html)
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "How many mighty men did David have?"

excerpts.excerpt_text: This number is correct, as there were three in the first class (Sa2 23:8-12), two in the second (Sa2 23:18-23), and thirty-two in the third (vv. 24-39), since Sa2 23:34 contains three names according to the amended text.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly affirms the stated total of thirty-seven and itemizes how it sums (3 + 2 + 32), resolving the missing-name shortfall via the three names read in the emended v.34 — the precise 36-vs-37 tension.

excerpts.excerpt_text: Of these shalishim we have here thirty-seven, and it can scarcely be said with propriety that we have thirty-seven out of thirty …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Reads 'thirty' (shalishim) as an office/corps title rather than a literal count, dissolving the 'thirty-seven out of thirty' label tension behind the number.

pd_work.resource: Keil & Delitzsch, Biblical Commentary on the Old Testament, on 2 Samuel 23:8, 39 (1861-75)
pd_work.author: Keil & Delitzsch
pd_work.note: Keil & Delitzsch treat this exact total at the verse, affirming 'thirty and seven in all' as correct and itemizing the count (3 + 2 + 32), with the apparent shortfall removed by the three names of the amended v.34.
